A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StreetCrafter. All 16 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original Waymo and PandaSet experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations in Tables 1–7, and qualitative synthesis and editing results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds qualitative results for a Wan2.1 adaptation and another deformable-object example.

M1.justification: Section 8.2 adds a substantially different model implementation using Wan2.1-14B-I2V: shared patch embeddings, zero-initialized linear LiDAR injection before transformer blocks, and LoRA training with pretrained weights frozen. This expands beyond the existing Vista U-Net implementation. Section 3.3 also revises the stated sampler from DDIM to Vista's EDM, without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: The named datasets and principal tasks remain Waymo/PandaSet street-view synthesis and editing. New Figure 11 extends qualitative coverage to adverse-weather and severe-occlusion scenes. The source and split of these additional examples are not specified.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same participants: 3DGS, EmerNeRF, Street Gaussians, UniSim, NeuRAD, ViewCrafter and DriveDreamer4D where previously evaluated. Wan is an alternative backbone for StreetCrafter, not an added independent baseline.

E3.justification: The added Wan experiment uses a 14B model with frozen-weight LoRA training. Figure 13 changes its stated camera displacement from 2 meters to a gradual 3-meter shift while retaining the same image panels; this is a reported setting revision, not evidence of a rerun. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds qualitative cases examining the Wan adaptation under severe occlusion and adverse weather, and expands the deformable-object illustration from one sequence in v2 Figure 16 to two in v3 Figure 17. The existing conditioning, distillation, sampling-ratio and noise-scale ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and averages across clips or scenes without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3 introduces no change to uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds Wan-generated results in Figure 11 and another pedestrian sequence in Figure 17. All numerical entries in Tables 1–7 and the reported DriveDreamer4D comparison values remain unchanged. The added visuals do not establish a quantitative performance gain under matched conditions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–10, including diffusion, Gaussian rendering and loss definitions, remain unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs accompany the Wan adaptation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about LiDAR-conditioned camera control, scene editing, dynamic-3DGS distillation and street-view synthesis performance.

C2.justification: New Section 8.2 attributes plausible synthesis in regions invisible to both camera and LiDAR to Wan's generative prior, and interprets the examples as supporting adaptation to stronger backbones. The deformable-object discussion also makes incorrect guidance from multi-frame LiDAR aggregation more explicit. The conclusion's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplies the Wan checkpoint identifier and implementation details about shared embeddings, zero initialization and frozen-weight LoRA. Wan-specific LoRA rank, learning rate and training budget are not provided. Existing Vista/3DGS implementation settings and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds the Wan reference and removes the DDIM reference, citing the already included EDM work in the revised sampling passage. The main related-work discussion and positioning against reconstruction and camera-control methods remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 inserts an appendix subsection about the Wan adaptation and renumbers subsequent subsections. It makes limited wording changes to sampling, interpolation and deformable-object passages, and fixes the noise-scale typo. The main narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figure 11, expands the deformable-object figure, and relocates and reformats v2's editing Figure 11 as Figure 14. Appendix figures and tables are rearranged, and Figure 13's caption changes. The main figures and numerical-table designs remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The Wan implementation and additional weather, occlusion and pedestrian examples provide useful evidence of broader applicability. The EDM wording also improves consistency with the existing Vista-based description. These are limited gains: the numerical evidence is unchanged, and the Wan extension lacks controlled quantitative comparisons and complete training settings.
